changed: The ERP simulator is the discovered provider plugin fixture-erp (R-2 part 2, ADR 0026, D2). fake_erp.py and scenarios.py moved with git mv from e_agent/erp/testing to e_agent/plugins/erp/simulator (git shows renames; fake_erp.py changes only in its import lines: the relative domain imports became e_agent.erp.* and ruff re-sorted them). The package adds plugin.py (create_plugin: settings scenario, default valid, and lose_response_after_commit, default false; an unknown setting, an unknown or non-string scenario, or a non-bool fault raises InvalidPluginSettings) and e_agent_plugin.json (kind provider, no capabilities, the 17 binding templates equal to fake_erp.BINDINGS, which a test asserts). plugins/ and plugins/erp/ are namespace directories without __init__.py. The new distribution dists/adapter-erp-simulator (e-agent-adapter-erp-simulator 0.1.0; contracts, plugin-sdk, domain-erp) declares the entry point fixture-erp; the root workspace lists it in the dev group and uv sources, and uv.lock adds only that member (20 lines, no third-party change). bootstrap.py no longer imports or registers the simulator: the hand-registered fixture block, the profile.fixture requirement and Runtime.fake_erp are gone, and a fixture profile admits fixture-erp like any plugin (allow_unverified_fixture as before). build_runtime and admit_plugins take plugin_settings (by plugin id, merged over the profile's settings) in place of scenario and lose_response_after_commit; overrides for a plugin the profile does not enable, or on a non-fixture profile, are refused with STARTUP_REJECTED. The SDK gains InvalidPluginSettings (sdk/errors.py) and PluginContribution.diagnostics; the registry turns a factory's InvalidPluginSettings into STARTUP_REJECTED naming the plugin, and keeps diagnostics hooks by plugin id; Runtime.diagnostics() returns them. The CLI no longer imports SCENARIOS: --scenario and --fault lost-response set the scenario and lose_response_after_commit settings on every enabled plugin whose profile entry names that setting, and are refused when none does; its JSON key fixture_erp_create_calls became provider_diagnostics ({"fixture-erp": {"create_calls": n}}). FixtureConfig.scenario stays (now optional, default none); the packaged fixture profile and profiles/dev-ollama.json enable fixture-erp 0.1.0 with explicit settings. Discovery (sdk/discovery.py) now walks namespace parents by their last name: a dotted PathFinder lookup of e_agent.plugins.erp needs e_agent.plugins in sys.modules and raised KeyError in a fresh process (found by test_live_profile_never_imports_simulator; regression test in tests/unit/sdk/test_discovery.py). Import contracts: the simulator is a root package in the provider layer, a source of the provider contract (no kernel, server or erp.testing), forbidden to the kernel, the domain pack and the infrastructure adapters; new contracts 'Server never imports the ERP simulator' and 'ERP providers are independent of each other' (odoo, simulator); mypy checks the package. check_wheels.py builds and smoke-tests the new wheel, asserts the domain-erp wheel no longer ships testing/fake_erp.py or scenarios.py, installs the simulator into the server venv for the installed demos (the server does not depend on it), and checks its pin with the others. Tests and scripts moved off rt.fake_erp (runtime.diagnostics(), registry.plugin_executors['fixture-erp']), the old imports and the old CLI key; scripts/qualify_model.py and scripts/release_report.py pass plugin_settings for fixture-erp. Red first: tests/unit/plugins/erp/simulator failed at collection with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'e_agent.plugins', and test_repo_layout failed on 10 dists and the missing plugins/ directory. Review fix (5d402aa, Codex review rework R-1 and R-2): InvalidPluginSettings now carries the setting name and a fixed reason, and the registry composes the operator message itself, showing a setting name only when it is a plain name (else '<unnamed setting>'), so no profile value reaches safe_message (the simulator's refusals no longer format any value); fixture.scenario follows the 1d.4 rule through bootstrap.fixture_scenario_check: on a fixture profile it must equal the scenario setting of every enabled plugin that takes one, a different value or a value no plugin takes is refused with STARTUP_REJECTED, and a profile written before 1d.5 (no fixture-erp entry) loads and is refused at startup with 'no enabled plugin takes the setting 'scenario' (from fixture.scenario)'. The takers helper (bootstrap.settings_for_takers) is shared with the CLI, whose no-taker refusal is now STARTUP_REJECTED.

Known limit: a plugin 'takes' a setting only when its profile entry names it, so a fixture profile that enables fixture-erp without an explicit settings.scenario can use neither --scenario nor fixture.scenario (both are refused, never dropped); both committed fixture profiles name it. A declared settings schema in the manifest would lift this

rulings.ruling: FixtureConfig.scenario stays in the profile schema (review R-2; the earlier ruling removed it, which the plan's Global Constraints and ADR 0026's 'existing local profiles keep loading' do not allow). It follows the 1d.4 rule: on a fixture profile it must equal the scenario setting of the enabled plugins that take one; a different value, or one no enabled plugin takes, is refused at startup. The server cannot move it into the plugin's settings without naming fixture-erp (1d.7 forbids 'erp' in server literals), so it is a consistency check, not a fold (plan ruling rewritten in the fix commit, ENG-PLAN-3)
rulings.cost_if_wrong: a profile written before 1d.5 loads but cannot start until it enables fixture-erp, which ADR 0026 requires anyway; startup names the cause

rulings.ruling: --scenario and --fault apply to every enabled plugin whose profile entry already names the setting, and are refused when none does; build_runtime takes plugin_settings by plugin id, accepted on fixture profiles only
rulings.cost_if_wrong: a fixture profile must list the setting for the CLI flag to reach the plugin (both committed fixture profiles do); a future plugin wanting CLI-driven settings would want a declared settings schema in its manifest instead

rulings.ruling: The create-call report comes from a diagnostics hook on PluginContribution (a closure in plugin.py), not a method on FakeErp, so the moved file stays verbatim apart from imports; the CLI key becomes provider_diagnostics, since 1d.7 forbids 'erp' in server literals
rulings.cost_if_wrong: consumers of the CLI JSON key fixture_erp_create_calls must read provider_diagnostics['fixture-erp']['create_calls']; every in-repo consumer is migrated

rulings.ruling: The registry catches only InvalidPluginSettings from a factory and refuses with STARTUP_REJECTED, composing the message from the setting name and the plugin's fixed reason (review R-1: the first version echoed the plugin's text, which carried the value); any other factory exception propagates as before. An unknown scenario was INVALID_REQUEST from bootstrap and is now STARTUP_REJECTED from admission
rulings.cost_if_wrong: a kernel diff, so the review goes to Codex; an operator no longer sees the rejected value in the startup error, only which setting and why

rulings.ruling: The scope was amended for src/e_agent/sdk/errors.py (the new exception) and src/e_agent/sdk/discovery.py (the nested-namespace fix), both recorded in the contract
rulings.cost_if_wrong: the discovery change touches every editable-install lookup; the existing discovery tests and every plugin's discovery in the full suite pass
